name: Pancreatic Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of abnormal arteriovenous shunting within the pancreas on angiography or contrast-enhanced imaging
Presence of gastrointestinal bleeding, abdominal pain, or pancreatitis symptoms consistent with pancreatic AVM
Exclusion of other causes of pancreatic vascular anomalies or tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological confirmation of pancreatic AVM plus compatible clinical symptoms with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities such as angiography, CT angiography, or MRI.

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic or acute gastrointestinal bleeding
Elevated serum amylase and lipase during pancreatitis episodes
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT showing early venous filling in pancreas
Digital subtraction angiography demonstrating arteriovenous shunting
MRI/MR angiography revealing vascular malformation within pancreas
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations identified
Usually sporadic; rare familial cases reported
other: Endoscopic ultrasound may identify abnormal vascular channels
Histopathology shows tangled arteries and veins without capillary bed

distinguishingFeatures: Benign vascular tumor with different imaging characteristics
Lack of direct arteriovenous shunting on angiography
Solid tumor with hormonal symptoms in some cases
No early venous filling or arteriovenous shunting on imaging
No abnormal vascular shunting on angiography

redFlags: Massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage causing hemodynamic instability
Rapidly enlarging abdominal mass with severe pain
